note: The comparison covers three American carriers and the four carriers of Nagumo’s strike force at Midway, 4–7 June 1942. Yorktown and all four Japanese carriers sank or were scuttled within that interval. Hosho with the distant main body, the Aleutian carriers, and Saratoga arriving later are not added to this carrier-battle cohort. Hammann, Mikuma and other non-carrier losses are outside its numerator and denominator. Original national participants are retained as explicitly unquantified other naval formations, excluding the named carriers. Separate unquantified air components acknowledge the central aircraft attacks without converting aircraft to ships or inventing a common-time aviation strength or loss total. The propeller-aircraft silhouette represents a typical component, not every aircraft type, sortie or air group. No human deaths are inferred. The new carrier model is a straight-deck family analogy; island placement, exhaust and exact hulls vary among the named ships, and the deck is deliberately empty rather than implying a complement. Source event coordinates remain broad locators, not the tactical positions or tracks of these dispersed forces. Formations and animation timing remain illustrative.
